correctness.summary: For gamma=1 the gap is exactly one. For gamma>=2, gamma_t2<=2gamma-1 and gamma_t2<=n/2 imply the fixed-order upper bound. The explicit broom-of-length-four-arms trees have gamma=d+1 and gamma_t2=2d+1, attaining d=floor((n-2)/4) for every n>=6; small orders are attained by stars. Exhaustive finite checks agree.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Foundational and subsequent semitotal-domination papers were checked, including the half-order bound, tree comparisons, and the later characterization of graphs with gamma_t2=n/2. Exact and synonymous searches did not locate the fixed-order maximum gap or the all-order extremal tree family. Because the upper bound is a short synthesis of known inequalities, a differently phrased prior corollary remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact fixed-order extremum over all connected graphs, shows the same extremum already occurs for trees, and supplies a uniform sharp construction at every order.

limitations: No classification of all extremal graphs or trees is claimed.
The theorem treats finite simple connected graphs only.
The upper-bound argument is a short optimization of established inequalities rather than a new half-order estimate.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; differently indexed domination literature may contain an equivalent corollary.
